dataIdInfo.idPurp: This North American Environmental Atlas base layer shows political entities in North America as polygons representing jurisdictional areas, and as lines representing political boundaries including International boundaries, Provincial boundaries and State or territory boundaries. This is a revised version of the 2010 data set released by the Commission for Environmental Cooperation. This new version integrates political boundaries spatial vector information published by each country in 2021. The data set includes 10 provinces and 3 territories in Canada; 32 states in Mexico; 48 states and the District of Columbia in the conterminous United Sates, Alaska and Hawaii, as well as Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands in the Caribbean region.
dataIdInfo.idAbs:
The North American Environmental Atlas data are standardized geospatial data. A variety of basic data layers (e.g. roads, railroads, populated places, political boundaries, hydrography, bathymetry, sea ice and glaciers) have been integrated so that their relative positions are correct. This collection of data sets forms a base with which other North American thematic data may be integrated. Any data outside of Canada, Mexico, and the United States of America included in the North American Atlas data sets is strictly to complete the context of the data.

The new version of the North American Environmental Atlas - Political Boundaries data set shows political entities in North America as polygons representing jurisdictional areas, such as, International boundaries, Provincial boundaries and State or territory boundaries.

This is a revised version of the 2010 data set released by the Commission for Environmental Cooperation. This new version integrates political boundaries spatial vector information published by each country in 2021. The data set includes 10 provinces and 3 territories in Canada; 32 states in Mexico; 48 states and the District of Columbia in the conterminous United Sates, Alaska and Hawaii, as well as Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands in the Caribbean region.

dataIdInfo.suppInfo:
The Commission for Environmental Cooperation (CEC) is an international organization created by Canada, Mexico, and the United States of America under the North American Agreement on Environmental Cooperation (NAAEC), which came into force at the same time as the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA). The CEC was established to address regional environmental concerns, help prevent potential trade and environmental conflicts, and to promote the effective enforcement of environmental law. As of 2020, the CEC operates in accordance with the Environmental Cooperation Agreement, which entered into force at the same time as the CUSMA/T-MEC/USMCA trade agreement.
This data set is available in several formats, including Shapefile, Map package, and a PDF Map, along with other files appropriate to particular format, such as .lyrx and .qlr files.

dataSource.srcDesc: The 2021 cartographic boundary shapefiles are simplified representations of selected geographic areas from the U.S. Census Bureau's Master Address File / Topologically Integrated Geographic Encoding and Referencing (MAF/TIGER) Database (MTDB). These boundary files are specifically designed for small-scale thematic mapping. When possible, generalization is performed with the intent to maintain the hierarchical relationships among geographies and to maintain the alignment of geographies within a file set for a given year. Geographic areas may not align with the same areas from another year. Some geographies are available as nation-based files while others are available only as state-based files. States and equivalent entities are the primary governmental divisions of the United States. In addition to the fifty states, the Census Bureau treats the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, and each of the Island Areas (American Samoa, the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, Guam, and the U.S. Virgin Islands) as the statistical equivalents of states for the purpose of data presentation.

dataSource.srcDesc: The Integrated Geostatistical Framework is a product that integrates vector information, attribute tables and catalogues. It shows the geostatistical division of the national territory in successive levels of disaggregation. This division is given by the so-called GEOSTATISTICAL LIMITS, which can coincide with the official political-administrative limits, which have legal support; however, those that do not have such support should be understood as provisional limits, drawn only to carry out census operations. These provisional limits do not claim to be official, given that the National Institute of Statistics and Geography is not the body empowered to define political-administrative limits.

prcStep.stepDesc:
1. Input vector spatial datasets by country were transformed to the CEC reference Lambert Azimuthal Equal Area projection. A set of new attributes matching some of the attributes from the last CEC Political Boundaries version (2006) were created for each national dataset. Additional attributes were added.
2. The coastline along Canada and Mexico was manually edited to eliminate long spatial connections from inner water bodies (rivers and inlets), identified as large gap areas within the continental region. The large empty areas inside each country were reclassified to the state polygons where they were spatially located.
3. An initial topology check-up was performed to ensure spatial consistency on each national dataset; gaps and overlapping areas were fixed. Processed national datasets were spatially integrated in a North American Political Boundaries map.
4. A second topology check-up was built at the North American level in order to ensure topological polygon structure. Small spatial gaps between national boundaries were fixed by means of assigning the class of the largest adjacent polygon. A similar approach was taken for small overlapping areas between country boundaries. No changes were applied over the Great Lakes of Nort America, yielding a large spatial gap in the area.

locale.idAbs: This reference map from the North American Environmental Atlas depicts political entities in North America, with jurisdictional areas represented as polygons and political boundaries, including international boundaries, and provincial, state, or territory boundaries, as lines. This revised map, which was previously released by the Commission for Environmental Cooperation in 2010, integrates spatial vector information on political boundaries published by each country in 2021. The dataset includes 10 provinces and three territories in Canada, 32 states in Mexico, and in the United States, 48 states and the District of Columbia in the conterminous United States, and the states Alaska and Hawaii, as well as Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands in the Caribbean region.

Este mapa de referencia del Atlas ambiental de América del Norte muestra las entidades políticas de América del Norte como polígonos que representan áreas jurisdiccionales, delimitados por líneas que representan los límites políticos: internacionales, estatales o provinciales y territoriales. Se trata de una versión revisada del mapa de 2010, publicado anteriormente por la Comisión para la Cooperación Ambiental. Esta nueva versión íntegra la información vectorial espacial correspondiente a límites políticos publicada por cada país en 2021. El conjunto de datos incluye 10 provincias y 3 territorios en Canadá; 32 estados en México, y en Estados Unidos: 48 estados y el Distrito de Columbia en la zona continental contigua, los estados de Alaska y Hawái, así como Puerto Rico y las Islas Vírgenes estadounidenses en la región del Caribe.

Cette carte de référence de l’Atlas environnemental de l’Amérique du Nord, montre les entités politiques de l’Amérique du Nord sous forme de polygones représentant les zones de compétence, ainsi que les frontières politiques représentées sous forme de lignes, y compris les frontières internationales, provinciales, étatiques et territoriales. Il s’agit d’une version révisée de la carte que la Commission de coopération environnementale (CCE) a publiée en 2010, et elle comporte des informations spatiales vectorielles sur les frontières politiques publiées par chaque pays en 2021. L’ensemble de données porte sur 10 provinces et 3 territoires au Canada et 32 États au Mexique, alors qu’aux États-Unis, il porte sur 48 États et le district de Columbia dans les États américains contigus, mais aussi les États de l’Alaska et d’Hawaï, Porto Rico et les îles Vierges américaines dans la région des Caraïbes.
